status.en: 10 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 25% more than the week before, most of them in Kuki, Yangon and Mandalay.
status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Kuki, Yangon og Mandalay.

summary.en: In the past week ten armed incidents were reported, 25% more than the previous week, mainly in Kuki, Mandalay and Yangon. None of these incidents were covered by multiple outlets. The UCDP recorded 2,332 battle‑related deaths in 2024. Reports describe civilians living in fear of being seized by the army, attacks killing at least five people and torching homes, and appeals urging ethnic armed groups to freeze maps and end the war. International attention includes sanctions being lifted on the daughter of a military‑linked businessman and regional diplomatic activity.
summary.nb: Den siste uken ble ti væpnede hendelser rapportert, 25 % flere enn uken før, hovedsakelig i Kuki, Mandalay og Yangon. Ingen av hendelsene ble dekket av flere medier. UCDP registrerte 2 332 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024. Rapporter beskriver sivile som lever i frykt for å bli tatt av hæren, angrep som drepte minst fem personer og brente ned hus, samt oppfordringer om at etniske væpnede grupper skal fryse kart og avslutte krigen. Internasjonal oppmerksomhet inkluderer at sanksjoner ble opphevet for datteren til en militær‑tilknyttet forretningsmann og regionalt diplomatisk engasjement.

background.extract: The Myanmar civil war began following the military coup on 1 February 2021. The seizure of power triggered mass anti-coup demonstrations and a violent crackdown by the Tatmadaw, which significantly escalated the country's longstanding insurgencies.
